records.source: Καὶ ἐκεῖθεν ἀναστὰς ἔρχεται εἰς τὰ ὅρια τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, καὶ συμπορεύονται πάλιν ὄχλοι πρὸς αὐτόν, καὶ ὡς εἰώθει πάλιν ἐδίδασκεν αὐτούς.
records.gloss: And from there having risen up he comes into the regions of Judea and beyond the Jordan, and come together again crowds to him, and as he was accustomed again he was teaching them.
pieces: Jesus set out from there and came to the districts of Judea and the land beyond the Jordan. Crowds came together around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} again, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} taught them once more, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} usually did.

L.1: And rising up from there, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes into the regions of Judea and beyond the Jordan, and crowds again come together to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was accustomed, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was again teaching them.

R.1: Jesus left Capernaum and went south to the land of Judea and to the area on the east side of the Jordan River. Again crowds of people came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. And Jesus taught them, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} always did.

decisions.choice: comes, come together: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: As often in Mark, past events are told in the present tense to make them vivid. The sense is past: he went, and the crowds gathered.

decisions.choice: the regions of Judea and beyond the Jordan: the land around Jerusalem and the land east of the river
decisions.reason: The land east of the Jordan was called Perea and was ruled by Herod Antipas. Jesus is now moving south toward Jerusalem (10:32).

decisions.choice: and beyond the Jordan
alternatives: through the region beyond the Jordan
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "through the region beyond the Jordan", which describes a route through Perea, and others leave out "and". The SBLGNT reads "and", naming two areas. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: from there: from Capernaum, where 9:33-50 took place
decisions.reason: The last place Mark names is the house in Capernaum (9:33).

decisions.choice: Capernaum; went south; the area on the east side of the Jordan River
decisions.reason: Readable names the place Jesus left and says where the land beyond the Jordan lay.

records.heading: What God has joined

records.source: Καὶ ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν εἰ ἔξεστιν ἀνδρὶ γυναῖκα ἀπολῦσαι, πειράζοντες αὐτόν.
records.gloss: And they were asking him if it is lawful for a husband a wife to divorce, testing him.
pieces: Some people asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} whether the law allows a husband to divorce his wife. They were trying to trap {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.2: And they were asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} if it is lawful for a husband to divorce a wife, testing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.2: Some people came to test Jesus. They asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Does God's law let a man divorce his wife?"

decisions.choice: they were asking him: the SBLGNT does not name the questioners
alternatives: Pharisees came and were asking him
decisions.reason: Most manuscripts read "Pharisees came up and asked him". A few early witnesses have only "they were asking him", and the SBLGNT follows them; the words about the Pharisees may have come in from Matthew 19:3. Either way, the question is put to test Jesus. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: testing: trying to trap him into a wrong or dangerous answer
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of Satan in 1:13 and of the Pharisees in 8:11. Herod Antipas had put John to death for speaking against his marriage (6:17-18), and Jesus is now in Herod's territory.

decisions.choice: is it lawful: does the law of Moses allow it
alternatives: is it legal under Roman law
decisions.reason: Jews of the time agreed that the law allowed a husband to divorce. They argued over the grounds. Asking whether it was allowed at all invited Jesus to set himself against Moses.

decisions.choice: were asking: an imperfect, they kept pressing the question
decisions.reason: The tense can describe a question pressed or repeated.

decisions.choice: Some people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply a subject, since the SBLGNT does not name who asked.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί ὑμῖν ἐνετείλατο Μωϋσῆς;
records.gloss: And he answering said to them, What you did command Moses?
pieces: He replied with a question: "What did Moses command you?"

L.3: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered and said to them, "What did Moses command you?"

R.3: Jesus answered them with a question. He said, "What did Moses tell you to do?"

decisions.choice: what did Moses command you: Jesus sends them back to the law
decisions.reason: Jesus answers with a question, as he does in 11:29-30. He uses the word "command"; in their reply they speak only of what Moses allowed (10:4).

decisions.choice: you: the questioners and Israel as a whole
decisions.reason: Moses gave the law to Israel, and Jesus speaks of it as given to them.

records.source: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Ἐπέτρεψεν Μωϋσῆς βιβλίον ἀποστασίου γράψαι καὶ ἀπολῦσαι.
records.gloss: And they said, Permitted Moses a roll of divorce to write and to send away.
pieces: They said, "Moses allowed a man to write out a certificate of divorce and send his wife away."

L.4: And they said, "Moses permitted [a man] to write a certificate of divorce and to send [her] away."

R.4: They answered, "Moses let a man write his wife a paper saying they were divorced. Then he could send her away."

decisions.choice: a certificate of divorce: the rule in Deuteronomy 24:1-4
alternatives: a law of Moses not found in the Scriptures
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 24:1 speaks of a husband who writes his wife a certificate of divorce and sends her out of his house. The passage takes divorce for granted and limits what may follow it.

decisions.choice: certificate of divorce: a written document that set the woman free to marry again
decisions.reason: The husband himself wrote and gave the document. It gave the woman proof that she was no longer his wife.

decisions.choice: permitted: allowed, not commanded
decisions.reason: Jesus asked what Moses commanded (10:3); they answer with what Moses allowed.

decisions.choice: [a man] ... [her] (L); a man, his wife (B, R)
alternatives: to write and to send away
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves the man and the woman to be understood. Literal brackets them; Balanced and Readable name them.

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πρὸς τὴν σκληροκαρδίαν ὑμῶν ἔγραψεν ὑμῖν τὴν ἐντολὴν ταύτην·
records.gloss: But Jesus said to them, Because of the hardness of heart of you he wrote for you the commandment this.
pieces: But Jesus told them, "It was because your hearts were hard that Moses wrote this commandment for you.

L.5: But Jesus said to them, "Because of your hardness of heart he wrote this commandment for you.

R.5: Jesus said to them, "Moses wrote that rule for you because you were stubborn and would not obey God.

decisions.choice: hardness of heart: stubborn unwillingness to obey God
decisions.reason: The word is used in the Greek of Deuteronomy 10:16 and Jeremiah 4:4 for a heart that will not turn to God. Mark speaks of hard hearts in 3:5 and 6:52.

decisions.choice: the commandment was given because of sin, not as God's ideal
alternatives: divorce is wrong in every case under the law
decisions.reason: Jesus does not deny that Moses wrote the rule. He says it was given to limit the harm done by people's hardness, while God's purpose is shown at creation (10:6-9).

decisions.choice: because of: on account of
decisions.reason: The preposition gives the reason the commandment was written.

decisions.choice: he wrote: Moses, named in 10:3-4
decisions.reason: The subject carries on from the previous verses.

decisions.choice: Moses
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Moses so that the subject is clear. Readable explains hardness of heart in plain words.

records.source: ἀπὸ δὲ ἀρχῆς κτίσεως ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ ἐποίησεν αὐτούς·
records.gloss: From however [the] beginning of creation male and female he made them.
pieces: But at the beginning, when the world was created, God made them male and female.

L.6: But from [the] beginning of creation {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made them male and female.

R.6: But when God first created the world, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made people male and female.

decisions.choice: male and female he made them: Genesis 1:27
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes Genesis 1:27 (and 5:2), which says God created humankind male and female.

decisions.choice: he made them: the SBLGNT does not name God
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "God" as the subject. The earliest leave it to be understood from the Genesis text. Either way God is the one who made them. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: from the beginning of creation: God's purpose from the start comes before the later rule
decisions.reason: Jesus sets what God did at creation above the permission given later in Deuteronomy.

decisions.choice: God made (B); God first created ... he made (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God, who is the subject in the Genesis text.

records.source: ἕνεκεν τούτου καταλείψει ἄνθρωπος τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν μητέρα καὶ προσκολληθήσεται πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔσονται οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν· ὥστε οὐκέτι εἰσὶν δύο ἀλλὰ μία σάρξ·
records.gloss: On account of this will leave a man the father of him and the mother and will be joined to the wife of him, \v 8 and will be the two into flesh one; therefore no longer they are two but one flesh.
pieces: 'This is why a man will leave his father and his mother and be joined to his wife,
and the two of them will be one flesh.' And so they are two no longer, but one flesh.

L.7: 'On account of this a man will leave his father and mother and will be joined to his wife,
L.8: and the two will become one flesh'; so they are no longer two, but one flesh.

R.7: God's word says, 'That is why a man leaves his father and mother and is joined to his wife.
R.8: The two of them will become one body.' So they are not two people anymore. They are one.

decisions.choice: Genesis 2:24, quoted from the Greek version
decisions.reason: Jesus joins Genesis 2:24 to Genesis 1:27. The quotation follows the Greek translation of Genesis, which has "the two"; the Hebrew has "they".

decisions.choice: and will be joined to his wife: in the SBLGNT text
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts lack these words. The eye of a copyist could easily skip from one "and" to the next, or the words could have been added from Matthew 19:5 and Genesis. Without them, "the two" in 8a has no clear antecedent. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: become one flesh: become a single, united person and family
decisions.reason: In Hebrew thought flesh means a human being or a family tie (Genesis 29:14). The union includes the body but is more than that.

decisions.choice: so they are no longer two: Jesus draws the conclusion from the quotation
decisions.reason: The quotation ends with "one flesh". The next words are Jesus' own.

decisions.choice: a man: a male person, here a husband
decisions.reason: Genesis speaks of a man leaving his parents to be joined to his wife.

decisions.choice: God's word says
decisions.reason: Readable shows that Jesus is quoting Scripture. It says "one body" and "they are one" for one flesh.

records.source: ὃ οὖν ὁ θεὸς συνέζευξεν ἄνθρωπος μὴ χωριζέτω.
records.gloss: What therefore God has joined together, man not let separate.
pieces: What God has yoked together, then, no human being is to separate."

L.9: So what God has joined together, let {{gender:no human|no man}} separate."

R.9: God has joined the two of them together. So no one should separate them."

decisions.choice: joined together: yoked together, as two animals under one yoke
decisions.reason: The verb pictures two animals sharing one yoke and working as one. God himself makes the union.

decisions.choice: man: any human being, a husband or anyone else
decisions.reason: The word is the general word for a human being. It sets human action against what God has done.

decisions.choice: what: neuter, the union itself
decisions.reason: The word points to the joined pair as one thing.

decisions.choice: yoked together
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture in the verb.

records.source: Καὶ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν πάλιν οἱ μαθηταὶ περὶ τούτου ἐπηρώτων αὐτόν.
records.gloss: And in the house again the disciples concerning this were asking him.
pieces: Back in the house, the disciples asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} about this again.

L.10: And in the house the disciples were again asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} about this.

R.10: Later, when they were inside the house, Jesus' followers asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} about what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said.

decisions.choice: in the house again: again in private, as in 7:17 and 9:28
decisions.reason: "Again" may go with "in the house" (once more in private) or with the asking. Mark often has the disciples ask Jesus in private.

decisions.choice: about this: about what Jesus taught on divorce
decisions.reason: They ask about the teaching of 10:2-9.

decisions.choice: followers
decisions.reason: Readable says "followers" for disciples, as in earlier chapters.

records.source: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ὃς ἂν ἀπολύσῃ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ γαμήσῃ ἄλλην μοιχᾶται ἐπ’ αὐτήν, καὶ ἐὰν αὐτὴ ἀπολύσασα τὸν ἄνδρα αὐτῆς γαμήσῃ ἄλλον μοιχᾶται.
records.gloss: And he says to them, Whoever shall divorce the wife of him and marry another commits adultery against her; \v 12 and if she having divorced the husband of her should marry another, she commits adultery.
pieces: He told them, "A man commits adultery against his wife if he divorces her and marries another woman.
And a woman who divorces her husband and marries another man commits adultery."

L.11: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "Whoever divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery against her;
L.12: and if she divorces her husband and marries another, she commits adultery."

R.11: Jesus said, "If a man divorces his wife and marries another woman, he is guilty of adultery against his first wife.
R.12: It is the same for a woman. If she divorces her husband and then marries another man, she is guilty of adultery."

decisions.choice: says: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present again.

decisions.choice: against her: against the first wife
decisions.reason: "Her" most likely refers to the wife he divorced: he wrongs her. It could refer to the new wife, with whom he commits adultery.

decisions.choice: if she divorces her husband: a wife's right under Greek and Roman law
alternatives: Jewish law gave women this right
decisions.reason: Under Jewish law only a husband could divorce. Greek and Roman law let a wife divorce her husband, and Herodias had left her first husband (6:17). Jesus' teaching applies to both.

decisions.choice: the man commits adultery against his wife: the husband is held to the same standard
alternatives: only a wife could be guilty of adultery
decisions.reason: In the custom of the time a man was thought to commit adultery only against another man's marriage. Jesus says a husband can wrong his own wife this way.

decisions.choice: if she divorces her husband and marries another
alternatives: if a woman leaves her husband and marries another
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts describe the woman as leaving or separating from her husband instead of divorcing him. The SBLGNT has the same verb as in 10:11. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: another woman; another man
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who is meant by "another". Readable also says whom the man wrongs, his first wife.

records.source: Καὶ προσέφερον αὐτῷ παιδία ἵνα αὐτῶν ἅψηται· οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ ἐπετίμησαν αὐτοῖς.
records.gloss: And they were bringing to him little children that them he might touch; but the disciples rebuked them.
pieces: People were bringing young children to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would touch them, but the disciples scolded them.

L.13: And they were bringing little children to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might touch them; but the disciples rebuked them.

R.13: People brought their young children to Jesus. They wanted {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to touch the children and bless them. But the followers told them off.

decisions.choice: touch: lay hands on them in blessing
decisions.reason: Parents asked respected teachers to bless their children by placing hands on them, as Jacob blessed Joseph's sons (Genesis 48:14). Jesus does this in 10:16.

decisions.choice: little children: young children, from infants to about twelve
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the twelve-year-old girl in 5:39-42.

decisions.choice: them: those who brought the children
decisions.reason: The disciples rebuke the people bringing the children, most likely their parents.

decisions.choice: were bringing: an imperfect, people kept coming
decisions.reason: The tense pictures a stream of people bringing children.

decisions.choice: and bless them
decisions.reason: Readable says what the touch was for, as 10:16 shows.

records.heading: Let the children come

records.source: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἠγανάκτησεν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἄφετε τὰ παιδία ἔρχεσθαι πρός με, μὴ κωλύετε αὐτά, τῶν γὰρ τοιούτων ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: Having seen now Jesus was indignant and said to them, Permit the little children to come to me, not do hinder them; for to such belongs the kingdom of God.
pieces: When Jesus saw this, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was angry and told them, "Allow the children to come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Do not try to stop them, because it is to people like them that the kingdom of God belongs.

L.14: But when Jesus saw [it], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was indignant and said to them, "Permit the little children to come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; do not hinder them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.

R.14: When Jesus saw what was happening, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was angry with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers. He said to them, "Let the children come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}! Do not keep them away. God's kingdom belongs to people who are like these children.

decisions.choice: was indignant: became angry at a wrong
decisions.reason: The word is a strong one. It is used of the ten in 10:41 and of those who objected to the anointing (14:4). Only here is it used of Jesus.

decisions.choice: to such belongs the kingdom of God: to the children and to people like them
decisions.reason: "Such" includes the children and all who are like them. 10:15 explains how.

decisions.choice: the kingdom belongs to those with nothing to offer
decisions.reason: Children had no rank or claim. Mark does not praise their innocence; the kingdom is given to those who receive it as a gift.

decisions.choice: angry
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a common word for this strong feeling.

decisions.choice: with his followers
decisions.reason: Readable says whom Jesus was angry with.

records.source: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὃς ἂν μὴ δέξηται τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ ὡς παιδίον, οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθῃ εἰς αὐτήν.
records.gloss: Truly I say to you, whoever not shall receive the kingdom of God as a child, no not shall enter into it.
pieces: Truly I tell you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God the way a child does will never get into it."

L.15: Truly I say to you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God as a child will never enter into it."

R.15: I tell you the truth: you must welcome God's kingdom the way a child would. If you do not, you will never enter it."

decisions.choice: as a child: as a child receives it
alternatives: as one would receive a child
decisions.reason: The words most likely mean receiving the kingdom the way a child does, with trust and empty hands. They could also mean receiving the kingdom as one welcomes a child (9:37).

decisions.choice: never: a double negative, a strong denial
decisions.reason: Two negatives together make the warning firm.

decisions.choice: receive the kingdom and enter it: the kingdom is both a gift now and a place to enter
decisions.reason: The kingdom is received now and entered in the end, as in 9:47 and 10:23-25.

decisions.choice: you must welcome ... If you do not
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to the hearer directly and splits the warning into two short sentences.

records.source: καὶ ἐναγκαλισάμενος αὐτὰ κατευλόγει τιθεὶς τὰς χεῖρας ἐπ’ αὐτά.
records.gloss: And having taken in arms them he was blessing, laying the hands on them.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the children in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} arms, laid {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands on them, and blessed them.

L.16: And taking them in [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] arms, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was blessing [them], laying [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] hands on them.

R.16: Then Jesus took the children in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} arms. He put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands on each of them and blessed them.

decisions.choice: was blessing: blessing warmly, a strengthened form of the verb
decisions.reason: Mark uses a strong form of the word for bless, found only here in the New Testament. Jesus gives more than the parents asked for.

decisions.choice: taking in arms: hugging, holding
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 9:36.

decisions.choice: was blessing: an imperfect, one child after another
decisions.reason: The tense pictures Jesus blessing them in turn.

decisions.choice: each of them
decisions.reason: Readable brings out the imperfect, blessing them one by one.

records.source: Καὶ ἐκπορευομένου αὐτοῦ εἰς ὁδὸν προσδραμὼν εἷς καὶ γονυπετήσας αὐτὸν ἐπηρώτα αὐτόν· Διδάσκαλε ἀγαθέ, τί ποιήσω ἵνα ζωὴν αἰώνιον κληρονομήσω;
records.gloss: And going forth of him into [the] road, having run up one and having knelt to him was asking him, Teacher good, what shall I do that life eternal I might inherit?
pieces: As Jesus was setting out on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} journey, a man ran up to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, fell on his knees in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and asked, "Good Teacher, what should I do to inherit eternal life?"

L.17: And as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was going out onto the road, someone ran up and knelt before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and was asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Good Teacher, what must I do so that I may inherit eternal life?"

R.17: Jesus was starting on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way again. Then a man ran up to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and kneeled down in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He asked, "Good Teacher, what do I have to do to receive eternal life from God?"

decisions.choice: eternal life: the life of the age to come
decisions.reason: Eternal life is the life God gives in the coming age (Daniel 12:2). In 10:30 Jesus speaks of it as belonging to "the age to come", and here it stands beside entering the kingdom of God (10:23-25).

decisions.choice: inherit: receive as a share given by God
decisions.reason: Israel inherited the land as God's gift. The man asks what he must do to receive his share in the life to come.

decisions.choice: ran up and knelt: eagerness and deep respect
decisions.reason: A man of wealth (10:22) would not usually run in public. Kneeling shows great respect for Jesus.

decisions.choice: someone: Mark says only "one"
decisions.reason: Mark does not say who he was. Matthew 19:20 calls him a young man and Luke 18:18 a ruler. Mark tells only later that he was rich.

decisions.choice: a man
decisions.reason: The word "one" is masculine, and 10:20-22 shows it was a man. Readable adds "from God" to show where eternal life comes from.

records.heading: A rich man's question

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Τί με λέγεις ἀγαθόν;
records.gloss: And Jesus said to him, Why me do you call good?
pieces: Jesus answered, "Why are you calling {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} good?

L.18: And Jesus said to him, "Why do you call {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} good?

R.18: Jesus answered, "Why do you say that I am good?

decisions.choice: why do you call me good: Jesus makes the man think about what he has said
alternatives: Jesus denies that he is good
Jesus rebukes the man for flattery
decisions.reason: Jesus does not say he is not good. He turns the man's attention to God, the source of all goodness. A reader may see that the one who is good is speaking with God's authority.

decisions.choice: good: good in the full sense, as God is good
decisions.reason: Calling a teacher "good" was very rare. Jesus takes the word seriously.

decisions.choice: Why do you say that I am good
alternatives: Why do you call me good
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plainer way to say the same thing.

records.source: οὐδεὶς ἀγαθὸς εἰ μὴ εἷς ὁ θεός.
records.gloss: No one good if not one, God.
pieces: No one is good except God alone.

L.18: No one [is] good except one, God.

R.18: Only God is good. No one else is.

decisions.choice: one, God: an echo of the Shema
decisions.reason: The words recall Deuteronomy 6:4, "the LORD is one", which Jesus quotes in 12:29. Only the one God is good in the full sense.

decisions.choice: except one, God: God alone
decisions.reason: The phrase means "except the one God" or "except God alone".

decisions.choice: Only God is good. No one else is.
alternatives: No one is good except God
decisions.reason: Readable states the positive first in two short sentences.

records.source: τὰς ἐντολὰς οἶδας· Μὴ φονεύσῃς, Μὴ μοιχεύσῃς, Μὴ κλέψῃς, Μὴ ψευδομαρτυρήσῃς, Μὴ ἀποστερήσῃς, Τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου καὶ τὴν μητέρα.
records.gloss: The commandments you know: Not you shall murder, not you shall commit adultery, not you shall steal, not you shall bear false witness, not you shall defraud, Honor the father of you and the mother.
pieces: You know what the commandments say: 'Do not murder. Do not commit adultery. Do not steal. Do not testify falsely. Do not cheat anyone. Honor your father and mother.'"

L.19: You know the commandments: 'Do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not bear false witness, do not defraud, honor your father and mother.'"

R.19: You know what God commands: 'Do not kill anyone. Do not commit adultery. Do not steal. Do not tell lies about other people in court. Do not cheat anyone. Respect your father and mother.'"

decisions.choice: the commandments: from the second half of the Ten Commandments
decisions.reason: Jesus lists commandments about how to treat other people (Exodus 20:12-16; Deuteronomy 5:16-20), and puts honoring parents last.

decisions.choice: do not defraud: not one of the Ten, but drawn from the law
decisions.reason: The law forbids holding back a worker's wages (Deuteronomy 24:14; Leviticus 19:13; Malachi 3:5). Jesus may use it in place of "do not covet", or because it fits a rich man.

decisions.choice: do not defraud: in the SBLGNT text
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts lack "do not defraud", perhaps because it is not one of the Ten Commandments or because Matthew and Luke lack it. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: bear false witness: give false evidence against someone
decisions.reason: The commandment is about testimony in court, though it came to cover lying in general.

decisions.choice: kill anyone; tell lies about other people in court; respect
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words. "Murder" is the precise word; Readable adds "anyone" to make clear it means killing another person, not all killing.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἔφη αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, ταῦτα πάντα ἐφυλαξάμην ἐκ νεότητός μου.
records.gloss: And he was saying to him, Teacher, these all I have kept from [the] youth of me.
pieces: "Teacher," he replied, "I have obeyed all of these since I was a boy."

L.20: And he said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, I have kept all these from my youth."

R.20: The man said, "Teacher, I have obeyed all these laws ever since I was young."

decisions.choice: youth: from boyhood, from the age a Jewish boy took on the law
decisions.reason: A Jewish boy became responsible for keeping the law around the age of thirteen.

decisions.choice: Teacher: this time without "good"
decisions.reason: The man drops the word "good" after Jesus' question in 10:18.

decisions.choice: I have kept all these: he believes he has obeyed them outwardly
decisions.reason: Jesus does not dispute his claim. Paul could say he was blameless as to the law's righteousness (Philippians 3:6).

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐμβλέψας αὐτῷ ἠγάπησεν αὐτὸν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἕν σε ὑστερεῖ· ὕπαγε ὅσα ἔχεις πώλησον καὶ δὸς τοῖς πτωχοῖς, καὶ ἕξεις θησαυρὸν ἐν οὐρανῷ, καὶ δεῦρο ἀκολούθει μοι.
records.gloss: And Jesus having looked at him loved him and said to him, One thing you is lacking; go, as much as you have sell and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven, and come follow me.
pieces: Jesus looked at him and loved him. "You are missing one thing," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told him. "Go and sell everything you own, and give the money to the poor. Then you will have treasure in heaven. After that, come and follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

L.21: And Jesus, looking at him, loved him and said to him, "One thing you lack: go, sell whatever you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

R.21: Jesus looked at the man and loved him. He said, "There is still one thing you need to do. Go and sell all you have. Give the money to poor people. Then you will have riches in heaven. And come, follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

decisions.choice: loved him: felt and showed love for him
decisions.reason: The verb is the common word for love. Mark alone says that Jesus loved him. His command comes from that love.

decisions.choice: looking at him: looking intently
decisions.reason: Mark uses this verb for a searching look (10:27; 14:67).

decisions.choice: treasure in heaven: riches kept by God
decisions.reason: Treasure in heaven is wealth that God keeps for a person and that cannot be lost (Matthew 6:20).

decisions.choice: the one thing lacking: to give up what holds him and follow Jesus
decisions.reason: The command to sell everything leads to the call "follow me". What he lacks is to follow Jesus with nothing held back.

decisions.choice: come, follow me: the SBLGNT ends here
alternatives: come, take up the cross, and follow me
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "take up the cross", most likely from 8:34. The earliest lack it. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: There is still one thing you need to do; riches
decisions.reason: Readable says what the lack means, and uses a plain word for treasure.

records.source: ὁ δὲ στυγνάσας ἐπὶ τῷ λόγῳ ἀπῆλθεν λυπούμενος, ἦν γὰρ ἔχων κτήματα πολλά.
records.gloss: And having been sad at the word he went away grieving; he was for having possessions many.
pieces: At these words his face clouded over, and he went away sad, for he owned a great deal of property.

L.22: But his face fell at the word, and he went away grieving, for he was [one] who had many possessions.

R.22: When the man heard this, he looked very unhappy. He went away sad, because he was very rich.

decisions.choice: his face fell: he became gloomy, his face darkened
decisions.reason: The word is used of a dark, stormy sky in Matthew 16:3. His face showed his dismay.

decisions.choice: possessions: property, especially land and houses
decisions.reason: The word means what one owns, often fields and estates.

decisions.choice: for he was one who had: the reason he went away
alternatives: a later comment with no link
decisions.reason: Only now does Mark tell the reader the man was wealthy, and it explains his grief.

decisions.choice: he was very rich
decisions.reason: Readable says what having many possessions means.

records.source: Καὶ περιβλεψάμενος ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Πῶς δυσκόλως οἱ τὰ χρήματα ἔχοντες εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσελεύσονται.
records.gloss: And having looked around Jesus says to the disciples of him, How difficultly those the riches having into the kingdom of God will enter!
pieces: Jesus looked around and told {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "How difficult it will be for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God!"

L.23: And looking around, Jesus says to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "How hard it will be for those who have riches to enter into the kingdom of God!"

R.23: Jesus looked around at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers. He said to them, "It is very hard for rich people to enter God's kingdom!"

decisions.choice: says: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present again.

decisions.choice: riches: money and wealth
decisions.reason: The word means money or property that can be used.

decisions.choice: how hard: wealth holds people back from the kingdom
alternatives: the rich are shut out by rule
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of difficulty here; 10:25-27 says it is impossible without God.

decisions.choice: looking around: as in 3:5 and 3:34, a look before a saying
decisions.reason: Mark uses the verb of Jesus looking around at those present before he speaks.

records.source: οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ ἐθαμβοῦντο ἐπὶ τοῖς λόγοις αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And the disciples were astonished at the words of him.
pieces: The disciples were amazed at what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said.

L.24: And the disciples were astonished at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} words.

R.24: The followers were very surprised at what Jesus said.

decisions.choice: were astonished: stunned, bewildered
decisions.reason: The word means a shocked surprise, as in 1:27. Many thought wealth was a sign of God's blessing (Deuteronomy 28:1-14), so Jesus' words overturned what they expected.

decisions.choice: were astonished: an imperfect, a lasting state
decisions.reason: The tense pictures their continuing bewilderment.

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς πάλιν ἀποκριθεὶς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τέκνα, πῶς δύσκολόν ἐστιν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσελθεῖν·
records.gloss: But Jesus again answering says to them, Children, how difficult it is into the kingdom of God to enter!
pieces: But Jesus said to them again, "My children, how hard it is to get into the kingdom of God!

L.24: But Jesus again responds and says to them, "Children, how hard it is to enter into the kingdom of God!

R.24: But Jesus said again, "My children, it is very hard to enter God's kingdom!

decisions.choice: children: a warm address to the disciples
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to grown men as a teacher or father speaks to his own. Only here in Mark does he call his disciples "children".

decisions.choice: how hard it is to enter: in the SBLGNT, said of everyone
alternatives: how hard it is for those who trust in riches to enter
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "for those who trust in riches", which limits the saying to the rich. The earliest lack it, and the shorter text is harder: it is hard for anyone to enter. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: answering says: speaks again in response
decisions.reason: The disciples have not spoken; Jesus responds to their astonishment.

decisions.choice: My children
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "my" to keep the warmth of the address.

records.source: εὐκοπώτερόν ἐστιν κάμηλον διὰ τῆς τρυμαλιᾶς τῆς ῥαφίδος διελθεῖν ἢ πλούσιον εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσελθεῖν.
records.gloss: Easier it is a camel through the eye of the needle to pass than a rich man into the kingdom of God to enter.
pieces: A camel could pass through the eye of a needle more easily than a rich person could enter the kingdom of God."

L.25: It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of the needle than for {{gender:a rich person|a rich man}} to enter into the kingdom of God."

R.25: A camel is a very big animal, and the hole in a needle is very small. But a camel could get through that hole more easily than a rich person could enter God's kingdom."

decisions.choice: a camel through the eye of a needle: something impossible
alternatives: a small gate in Jerusalem called the needle
decisions.reason: The largest animal in the land and the smallest opening make a picture of what cannot happen. There is no early evidence for a gate called the needle's eye; that idea came much later. 10:27 shows that Jesus means it is impossible for people.

decisions.choice: camel
decisions.reason: A few late manuscripts read a similar Greek word meaning a ship's rope, which softens the picture. The SBLGNT and nearly all manuscripts read "camel". Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: a rich man: anyone who is rich
decisions.reason: The word is masculine in form but speaks of rich people in general.

decisions.choice: A camel is a very big animal, and the hole in a needle is very small
alternatives: a camel through the eye of the needle
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture so that young readers see the point.

records.source: οἱ δὲ περισσῶς ἐξεπλήσσοντο λέγοντες πρὸς ἑαυτούς· Καὶ τίς δύναται σωθῆναι;
records.gloss: And exceedingly they were astonished saying to themselves, And who is able to be saved?
pieces: They were utterly amazed and said to each other, "Who can be saved, then?"

L.26: And they were exceedingly astonished, saying to one another, "Then who can be saved?"

R.26: The followers were even more surprised. They said to each other, "Then who can be saved?"

decisions.choice: be saved: be rescued by God and given life in his kingdom
decisions.reason: Here being saved means the same as entering the kingdom and inheriting eternal life (10:17, 23).

decisions.choice: then: if even the rich cannot, who can
decisions.reason: The word draws a conclusion from what Jesus said.

decisions.choice: saying to one another
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "saying to him", so that the disciples ask Jesus. The SBLGNT reads "to themselves", that is, to one another. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: The followers were even more surprised
decisions.reason: Readable names who was amazed and links this to 10:24.

records.source: ἐμβλέψας αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει· Παρὰ ἀνθρώποις ἀδύνατον ἀλλ’ οὐ παρὰ θεῷ, πάντα γὰρ δυνατὰ παρὰ τῷ θεῷ.
records.gloss: Having looked at them Jesus says, With men impossible, but not with God; all things for possible with God.
pieces: Jesus looked straight at them and said, "For human beings it cannot be done, but not for God. God can do anything."

L.27: Looking at them, Jesus says, "With {{gender:people|men}} [it is] impossible, but not with God; for all things are possible with God."

R.27: Jesus looked at them and said, "People cannot do this. But God can. God can do everything."

decisions.choice: all things are possible with God: the faith of Israel's Scriptures
decisions.reason: The words recall Genesis 18:14, "Is anything too hard for the LORD?", said when Sarah was promised a son, and Job 42:2.

decisions.choice: impossible with people, not with God: salvation is God's work
alternatives: the rich can save themselves with effort
decisions.reason: No one, rich or poor, can enter by human power. God alone can bring them in.

decisions.choice: says: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present again.

decisions.choice: God can do anything (B); God can do everything (R)
alternatives: all things are possible with God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say the same thing with God as the subject.

records.source: Ἤρξατο λέγειν ὁ Πέτρος αὐτῷ· Ἰδοὺ ἡμεῖς ἀφήκαμεν πάντα καὶ ἠκολουθήκαμέν σοι.
records.gloss: Began to say Peter to him, Behold, we have left all and have followed you.
pieces: Peter spoke up: "Look, we have left everything behind to follow {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

L.28: Peter began to say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Look, we have left everything and have followed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

R.28: Then Peter said to Jesus, "Look at us! We have left everything we had, and we have followed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

decisions.choice: have left, have followed: perfects, a step taken that still holds
decisions.reason: The tense shows a decision made in the past that continues. Peter contrasts the disciples with the rich man.

decisions.choice: look: calls attention to what follows
decisions.reason: The word draws attention to what Peter is about to say.

decisions.choice: we have left everything: as Peter and Andrew left their nets (1:18)
decisions.reason: James and John left their father in the boat (1:20) and Levi left his tax booth (2:14).

records.source: ἔφη ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐδείς ἐστιν ὃς ἀφῆκεν οἰκίαν ἢ ἀδελφοὺς ἢ ἀδελφὰς ἢ μητέρα ἢ πατέρα ἢ τέκνα ἢ ἀγροὺς ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ καὶ ἕνεκεν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου, ἐὰν μὴ λάβῃ ἑκατονταπλασίονα νῦν ἐν τῷ καιρῷ τούτῳ οἰκίας καὶ ἀδελφοὺς καὶ ἀδελφὰς καὶ μητέρας καὶ τέκνα καὶ ἀγροὺς μετὰ διωγμῶν, καὶ ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τῷ ἐρχομένῳ ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
records.gloss: Was saying Jesus, Truly I say to you, no one there is who has left house or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or lands for the sake of me and for the sake of the gospel, \v 30 if not he shall receive a hundredfold now in the time this, houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and lands, with persecutions, and in the age the coming life eternal.
pieces: Jesus said, "Truly I tell you, anyone who has left a home, brothers or sisters, mother or father, children or land because of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and because of the gospel

will receive a hundred times as much now, in this present time: homes, brothers, sisters, mothers, children and land, together with persecutions. And in the age that is coming they will receive eternal life.

L.29: Jesus said, "Truly I say to you, there is no one who has left house or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or fields for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sake and for the sake of the gospel
L.30: who will not receive a hundredfold now in this time, houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and fields, with persecutions, and in the age to come eternal life.

R.29: Jesus said, "I tell you the truth: some people have left their homes, brothers, sisters, mother, father, children or farms because of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and the good news.
R.30: Every one of them will get a hundred times as much in this life. They will have homes, brothers, sisters, mothers, children and farms. People will also treat them cruelly for following {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. And in the world to come they will have eternal life.

decisions.choice: a hundredfold now: a new family and shared homes among Jesus' followers
alternatives: great personal wealth in this life
decisions.reason: Jesus has already called those who do God's will his brother and sister and mother (3:34-35). Those who leave family find a far larger family among his followers, who share their homes.

decisions.choice: mothers, but not fathers: the second list leaves out fathers
decisions.reason: The new family has mothers, but Jesus does not name fathers. It may be because God alone is Father in this family (11:25; Matthew 23:9). Mark does not explain.

decisions.choice: persecutions: harassment and suffering for following Jesus
decisions.reason: Jesus does not promise ease. The gift of the new family comes with suffering, as in 4:17 and 13:9-13.

decisions.choice: the age to come, eternal life: the life of God's coming age
decisions.reason: Jews spoke of this age and the age to come. Eternal life belongs to the age to come, and it answers the man's question in 10:17.

decisions.choice: mother or father: the SBLGNT list has no wife
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts add "or wife" to the first list, as in Luke 18:29. The earliest lack it. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: no one who ... who will not receive: everyone who has left will receive
decisions.reason: The double negative makes a firm promise to all who have left these things.

decisions.choice: anyone who has left ... will receive (B); some people have left ... Every one of them will get (R)
alternatives: there is no one who has left ... who will not receive
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the double negative into a positive promise. Readable splits the long sentence and says what persecutions are.

records.source: πολλοὶ δὲ ἔσονται πρῶτοι ἔσχατοι καὶ οἱ ἔσχατοι πρῶτοι.
records.gloss: Many however will be first last and the last first.
pieces: Yet many who are first will end up last, and the last first."

L.31: But many [who are] first will be last, and the last first."

R.31: But many people who are important now will be the least important then. And many who are the least important now will be the most important."

decisions.choice: first and last: God reverses human ranking
alternatives: a rule about lines or order
decisions.reason: Those honored now, like the rich, may be last in the kingdom, and those who gave up everything may be first. The saying may also warn the disciples not to count on their own place.

decisions.choice: first last: the first will be last
decisions.reason: The verb "will be" links each pair: the first become last, the last become first.

decisions.choice: important now ... least important then
decisions.reason: Readable says what first and last mean and when the change comes.

records.source: Ἦσαν δὲ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ἀναβαίνοντες εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, καὶ ἦν προάγων αὐτοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἐθαμβοῦντο, οἱ δὲ ἀκολουθοῦντες ἐφοβοῦντο.
records.gloss: They were then on the road going up to Jerusalem, and was going on before them Jesus, and they were astonished, and those following were afraid.
pieces: They were on the road going up to Jerusalem, with Jesus going on ahead of them. The disciples were astonished, and the others who followed were afraid.

L.32: And they were on the road going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was going ahead of them, and they were astonished, and those who followed were afraid.

R.32: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers were on the road going up to Jerusalem. Jesus was walking out in front of them. The disciples were amazed at this. The others who were following were afraid.

decisions.choice: going up to Jerusalem: Jerusalem stands high in the hills
decisions.reason: Travelers always went up to Jerusalem, which lies high in the hills of Judea. Pilgrims coming to the Passover took the road from Jericho (10:46).

decisions.choice: they were astonished, those who followed were afraid: perhaps two groups
alternatives: one group, the disciples, both amazed and afraid
decisions.reason: Mark may mean the disciples were amazed while others in the crowd following were afraid. He may also be describing the same people in two ways.

decisions.choice: Jesus was going ahead of them: he leads the way to his suffering
alternatives: he was walking alone by chance
decisions.reason: Jesus walks in front, knowing what waits in Jerusalem (8:31; 9:31). His resolve amazes and frightens those behind him.

decisions.choice: The disciples ... the others who followed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the two groups as Mark seems to mean them. This follows the more likely reading.

records.heading: On the road up to Jerusalem

records.source: καὶ παραλαβὼν πάλιν τοὺς δώδεκα ἤρξατο αὐτοῖς λέγειν τὰ μέλλοντα αὐτῷ συμβαίνειν ὅτι Ἰδοὺ ἀναβαίνομεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδοθήσεται τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ τοῖς γραμματεῦσιν, καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτὸν θανάτῳ καὶ παραδώσουσιν αὐτὸν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν καὶ ἐμπαίξουσιν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐμπτύσουσιν αὐτῷ καὶ μαστιγώσουσιν αὐτὸν καὶ ἀποκτενοῦσιν, καὶ μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἀναστήσεται.
records.gloss: And having taken again the twelve he began them to tell the things being about him to happen, \v 33 Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and to the scribes, and they will condemn him to death and will hand over him to the Gentiles, \v 34 and they will mock him and will spit upon him and will flog him and will kill, and after three days he will rise.
pieces: Again {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the Twelve with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and began telling them the things that were about to happen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

"We are on our way up to Jerusalem," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "and there the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and scribes, who will condemn {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death and hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to the Gentiles.

They will make fun of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, spit on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, whip {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; and three days later {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rise."

L.32: And taking the twelve aside again, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to tell them the things that were about to happen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}:
L.33: "Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes, and they will condemn {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death and will hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to the Gentiles,
L.34: and they will mock {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and spit on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and flog {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and kill [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], and after three days {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rise."

R.32: Jesus took the Twelve away from the others again. He began to tell them the things that would soon happen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
R.33: He said, "Listen! We are going up to Jerusalem. There the Son of Man will be handed over to the leading priests and the teachers of God's law. They will decide that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} must die. Then they will hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to the Romans, who are not Jews.
R.34: They will laugh at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and spit on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They will beat {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with whips and kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But three days later {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will come back to life."

decisions.choice: the third prediction of the passion: the fullest of the three
decisions.reason: Jesus has foretold his death and rising in 8:31 and 9:31. This time he names Jerusalem, the chief priests and scribes, the Gentiles, and the mocking, spitting and flogging. Each is told in 14:53-15:20.

decisions.choice: handed over: delivered up, first to the Jewish leaders, then by them to the Gentiles
decisions.reason: The same verb is used twice: the Son of Man is handed over to the chief priests and scribes, and they hand him over to the Gentiles (15:1).

decisions.choice: the Gentiles: the Roman governor and his soldiers
decisions.reason: The word means the nations, people who are not Jews. Here it means the Roman rulers, who alone could carry out a death sentence (15:1-20).

decisions.choice: after three days
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "on the third day", the wording of Matthew 20:19 and Luke 18:33. The SBLGNT reads "after three days", as Mark has it in 8:31 and 9:31. Both mean the same. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: taking aside: taking with him apart from the others
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the Twelve alone, away from those who were following.

decisions.choice: kill: the Greek leaves "him" to be understood
decisions.reason: The object is clear from the verbs before it.

decisions.choice: handed over
decisions.reason: All levels say "handed over", as in 9:31, since the verb is wider than betrayal and is used for both steps here.

decisions.choice: the Romans, who are not Jews; come back to life
decisions.reason: Readable says who the Gentiles were in this case and what rising means.

records.source: Καὶ προσπορεύονται αὐτῷ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωάννης οἱ υἱοὶ Ζεβεδαίου λέγοντες αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, θέλομεν ἵνα ὃ ἐὰν αἰτήσωμέν σε ποιήσῃς ἡμῖν.
records.gloss: And come up to him James and John the sons of Zebedee saying to him, Teacher, we desire that whatever we might ask you you would do for us.
pieces: Then James and John, Zebedee's sons, came up to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. "Teacher," they said, "we would like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to do whatever we ask of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

L.35: And James and John, the sons of Zebedee, come up to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, we want {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to do for us whatever we ask {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

R.35: Then James and John, the two sons of Zebedee, came to Jesus. They said, "Teacher, please do for us whatever we ask."

decisions.choice: come up: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present again.

decisions.choice: whatever we ask: an open request for a favor
decisions.reason: Right after Jesus has spoken of his death (10:33-34), the two ask for honor for themselves. The request is like Herod's open promise in 6:22-23.

decisions.choice: James and John: two of the first four called (1:19-20)
alternatives: other men named James and John
decisions.reason: With Peter they saw the raising of Jairus's daughter (5:37) and the transfiguration (9:2). Jesus named them Boanerges, sons of thunder (3:17).

decisions.choice: please do for us whatever we ask
alternatives: we want you to do for us whatever we ask you
decisions.reason: Readable puts the request in a simple form.

records.heading: Not to be served but to serve

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί θέλετε ποιήσω ὑμῖν;
records.gloss: And he said to them, What do you desire I should do for you?
pieces: "What would you like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do for you?" {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them.

L.36: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "What do you want {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do for you?"

R.36: Jesus asked them, "What would you like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do for you?"

decisions.choice: what do you want me to do for you: the same question Jesus asks Bartimaeus (10:51)
decisions.reason: Mark sets the two answers side by side. The brothers ask for glory; the blind man asks to see.

decisions.choice: want ... I should do: Jesus does not promise until he hears the request
alternatives: he agrees to do whatever they ask
decisions.reason: He asks them to say what they want before he answers.

records.source: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Δὸς ἡμῖν ἵνα εἷς σου ἐκ δεξιῶν καὶ εἷς ἐξ ἀριστερῶν καθίσωμεν ἐν τῇ δόξῃ σου.
records.gloss: And they said to him, Grant to us that one of you at right and one at left we might sit in the glory of you.
pieces: They answered, "Grant that when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory, one of us may sit on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right and one on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} left."

L.37: And they said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Grant us that we may sit, one at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right and one at [{{deity_pronoun:your|Your}}] left, in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory."

R.37: They answered, "When {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} rule as King in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory, let one of us sit at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right side and the other at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} left side."

decisions.choice: at your right and at your left: the places of highest honor beside a king
decisions.reason: The seat at a king's right hand was the place of greatest honor and power (1 Kings 2:19; Psalm 110:1), and the left the next.

decisions.choice: your glory: the glory of the Son of Man when he comes as king
decisions.reason: Jesus has spoken of the Son of Man coming in the glory of his Father (8:38). The brothers expect him to rule soon.

decisions.choice: the request misunderstands Jesus' path
decisions.reason: They believe Jesus will reign, but they have not grasped that his way to glory is through death (10:33-34). At the cross the places at his right and left are taken by two rebels (15:27).

decisions.choice: When you rule as King in your glory
decisions.reason: Readable says what the brothers expect Jesus' glory to be.

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐκ οἴδατε τί αἰτεῖσθε· δύνασθε πιεῖν τὸ ποτήριον ὃ ἐγὼ πίνω, ἢ τὸ βάπτισμα ὃ ἐγὼ βαπτίζομαι βαπτισθῆναι;
records.gloss: And Jesus said to them, Not you know what you ask. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink, or the baptism that I am baptized to be baptized?
pieces: Jesus said to them, "You have no idea what you are asking for. Can you drink the cup that I am drinking, or be baptized with the baptism I am going through?"

L.38: But Jesus said to them, "You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink, or to be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?"

R.38: Jesus said to them, "You do not understand what you are asking. I must drink a cup of suffering. Can you drink it? I must go through a baptism of suffering. Can you go through it?"

decisions.choice: the cup: the suffering God gives him to bear
alternatives: a cup of wine at a feast
decisions.reason: In the prophets the cup stands for God's judgment, which the wicked must drink (Isaiah 51:17; Jeremiah 25:15; Psalm 75:9). In Gethsemane Jesus prays that this cup may be taken from him (14:36).

decisions.choice: the baptism: being overwhelmed by suffering, as by deep water
alternatives: the rite of baptism in water
decisions.reason: The verb means to be plunged under. The Psalms speak of trouble as floods that cover a person (Psalm 69:2-3; 42:8). Luke 12:50 has a similar saying about Jesus' death.

decisions.choice: drink, am baptized: present tenses, the suffering already begun or certain
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of his suffering as already under way.

decisions.choice: a cup of suffering; a baptism of suffering
decisions.reason: Readable says what the cup and the baptism stand for, which the other levels leave as pictures.

records.source: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Δυνάμεθα.
records.gloss: And they said to him, We are able.
pieces: "We can," they told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.39: And they said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "We are able."

decisions.choice: we are able: a confident answer that they do not yet understand
alternatives: they know exactly what he means
decisions.reason: When Jesus is arrested, all the disciples run away (14:50).

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τὸ ποτήριον ὃ ἐγὼ πίνω πίεσθε καὶ τὸ βάπτισμα ὃ ἐγὼ βαπτίζομαι βαπτισθήσεσθε, τὸ δὲ καθίσαι ἐκ δεξιῶν μου ἢ ἐξ εὐωνύμων οὐκ ἔστιν ἐμὸν δοῦναι, ἀλλ’ οἷς ἡτοίμασται.
records.gloss: And Jesus said to them, The cup that I drink you will drink, and the baptism that I am baptized you will be baptized; \v 40 but to sit at right of me or at left not is mine to give, but for whom it has been prepared.
pieces: Jesus told them, "The cup I drink, you will drink, and with the baptism I am going through you too will be baptized.
But a seat at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right or at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} left is not mine to grant. Those places belong to the ones for whom they have been prepared."

L.39: And Jesus said to them, "The cup that I drink you will drink, and with the baptism with which I am baptized you will be baptized;
L.40: but to sit at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right or at [{{deity_pronoun:my|My}}] left is not {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}} to give, but [it is] for those for whom it has been prepared."

R.39: Then Jesus said to them, "You will drink from the same cup of suffering as I do. You will go through the same baptism of suffering.
R.40: But I am not the one who chooses who will sit at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right side or at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} left side. God has prepared those places for the people he has chosen."

decisions.choice: you will drink, you will be baptized: they will share his suffering
decisions.reason: Jesus promises them suffering, not seats of honor. Acts 12:2 tells that Herod Agrippa put James to death with the sword.

decisions.choice: has been prepared: a passive, God is the one who prepared it
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the actor unnamed, a common way of speaking of God's action. Matthew 20:23 says "by my Father".

decisions.choice: at my right or left: perhaps pointing ahead to the cross
decisions.reason: In 15:27 two rebels are crucified with Jesus, one on his right and one on his left. Mark may want readers to see the irony.

decisions.choice: God has prepared those places for the people he has chosen
alternatives: for whom it has been prepared
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who prepares, as the passive implies.

records.source: Καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ δέκα ἤρξαντο ἀγανακτεῖν περὶ Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰωάννου.
records.gloss: And having heard the ten began to be indignant about James and John.
pieces: When the other ten heard about this, they became angry with James and John.

L.41: And when the ten heard [it], they began to be indignant about James and John.

R.41: The other ten followers heard about this. They were angry with James and John.

decisions.choice: be indignant: angry at what they felt was wrong
decisions.reason: The same word is used of Jesus in 10:14.

decisions.choice: the ten were angry: they wanted the same honor
decisions.reason: Their anger shows they too were thinking of rank, as in 9:34. Jesus speaks to all twelve in 10:42-45.

decisions.choice: the other ten
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that the ten are the rest of the Twelve.

records.source: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος αὐτοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Οἴδατε ὅτι οἱ δοκοῦντες ἄρχειν τῶν ἐθνῶν κατακυριεύουσιν αὐτῶν καὶ οἱ μεγάλοι αὐτῶν κατεξουσιάζουσιν αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: And having called near them Jesus says to them, You know that those being accounted to rule the Gentiles exercise lordship over them, and the great ones of them exercise authority over them.
pieces: Jesus called them to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and told them, "You know that those who are thought of as rulers of the nations lord it over their people, and their important men use their power over them.

L.42: And calling them to [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], Jesus says to them, "You know that those who are considered rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.

R.42: Jesus called them all together and said, "You know how it is with the people who rule over the nations. They like to show that they are the masters. Their leaders use their power to control people.

decisions.choice: considered: those who are thought to rule, or recognized as rulers
alternatives: those who only pretend to rule
decisions.reason: The word can simply mean recognized. It may also hint that their rule is only apparent, since God is the true ruler.

decisions.choice: lord it over, exercise authority over: rule harshly, using power for themselves
decisions.reason: Both verbs are strengthened forms that suggest power used against those under it.

decisions.choice: the Gentiles: the nations of the world and their rulers
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of the way kings and governors of the nations rule, as Rome ruled at that time.

decisions.choice: says: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present again.

decisions.choice: They like to show that they are the masters
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom.

records.source: οὐχ οὕτως δέ ἐστιν ἐν ὑμῖν· ἀλλ’ ὃς ἂν θέλῃ μέγας γενέσθαι ἐν ὑμῖν, ἔσται ὑμῶν διάκονος, καὶ ὃς ἂν θέλῃ ἐν ὑμῖν εἶναι πρῶτος, ἔσται πάντων δοῦλος·
records.gloss: Not thus however it is among you; but whoever desires great to become among you will be your servant, \v 44 and whoever desires among you to be first will be of all slave.
pieces: That is not how it is among you. Instead, whoever among you wants to become great must be your servant,
and whoever among you wants to be first must serve everyone as a slave.

L.43: But it is not so among you; but whoever wants to become great among you will be your servant,
L.44: and whoever wants to be first among you will be slave of all.

R.43: But it is not like that with you. If you want to be great, you must serve the others.
R.44: If you want to be first, you must be a slave to everyone.

decisions.choice: it is not so: a present, the way things are among Jesus' followers
decisions.reason: Jesus states what is true of his community. Some manuscripts have the future "it shall not be", which makes it a command.

decisions.choice: servant: one who waits on others
decisions.reason: The word is the one in 9:35. It is used of those who serve at table.

decisions.choice: slave: one owned by another, with no rights of his own
decisions.reason: The word is stronger than servant. A slave belonged to a master and had no standing. Jesus asks those who would be first to take the lowest place of all.

decisions.choice: will be: a future that works as a command
decisions.reason: As in 9:35, the future states what must be.

decisions.choice: must be
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the force of command.

decisions.choice: If you want to be great
alternatives: whoever wants to become great among you
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to the hearers directly, as in 9:35.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where the word for slave stands against the word for servant in one saying: the step down from servant to slave is the point (m3).

records.source: καὶ γὰρ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἦλθεν διακονηθῆναι ἀλλὰ διακονῆσαι καὶ δοῦναι τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ λύτρον ἀντὶ πολλῶν.
records.gloss: Even for the Son of Man not came to be served but to serve and to give the life of him a ransom for many.
pieces: The Son of Man {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} came, not so that others would serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but to serve them and to give {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life as the ransom price for many."

L.45: For even the Son of Man did not come to be served but to serve, and to give {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life [as] a ransom for many."

R.45: The Son of Man {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} did not come so that people would serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He came to serve others. He came to give {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life as a ransom, the price paid to set many people free."

decisions.choice: ransom: the price paid to set a slave or prisoner free
alternatives: a fee paid to the devil
decisions.reason: The word was used of money paid to free a slave or captive (Leviticus 25:51-52) and of a payment that saved a life that was forfeit (Exodus 21:30; 30:12). Jesus gives his own life as that price. Mark does not say to whom it is paid.

decisions.choice: for: in place of, instead of
decisions.reason: The preposition commonly means in exchange for, or in place of. His life is given in place of theirs.

decisions.choice: many: a great number, set against the one who gives his life
decisions.reason: In Hebrew thought "many" can mean the great multitude, with no thought of leaving others out. The contrast is between the one and the many, as in Isaiah 53:11-12 and Romans 5:15-19.

decisions.choice: to give his life a ransom for many: the suffering servant of Isaiah 53
decisions.reason: Isaiah 53:10-12 says the servant's life is made an offering for sin, that he pours out his life to death and bears the sin of many. Jesus speaks of himself as that servant.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man came to serve: a reversal of Daniel 7:14
decisions.reason: In Daniel 7:13-14 the one like a son of man is given a kingdom, and all peoples serve him. Jesus says the Son of Man came first to serve.

decisions.choice: life: his whole self, his life given up in death
alternatives: his soul as distinct from his body
decisions.reason: The word can mean soul or self; here, as in 8:35, it means a person's life.

decisions.choice: the ransom price
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "price" so that the meaning of ransom is clear.

decisions.choice: a ransom, the price paid to set many people free
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a ransom is in a short added phrase.

records.source: Καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς Ἰεριχώ.
records.gloss: And they come to Jericho.
pieces: Then they came to Jericho.

R.46: Then Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers came to the city of Jericho.

decisions.choice: Jericho: an old city near the Jordan, about fifteen miles from Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Jericho lies in the Jordan valley, far below Jerusalem. Pilgrims from Galilee and Perea passed through it on the steep road up to the city.

decisions.choice: come: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present again.

decisions.choice: Jesus and his followers; the city of
decisions.reason: Readable names who came and says what Jericho was.

records.heading: Blind Bartimaeus

records.source: καὶ ἐκπορευομένου αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ Ἰεριχὼ καὶ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ ὄχλου ἱκανοῦ ὁ υἱὸς Τιμαίου Βαρτιμαῖος τυφλὸς προσαίτης ἐκάθητο παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν.
records.gloss: And as was going out he from Jericho and the disciples of him and a crowd large, the son of Timaeus Bartimaeus, blind beggar, was sitting beside the road.
pieces: As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was going out of Jericho with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and a large crowd, Bartimaeus son of Timaeus, a blind beggar, was sitting beside the road.

L.46: And as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was going out from Jericho with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and a large crowd, the son of Timaeus, Bartimaeus, a blind beggar, was sitting beside the road.

R.46: As Jesus was leaving the city with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers and a big crowd, a blind man was sitting beside the road. He was begging. His name was Bartimaeus, which means son of Timaeus.

decisions.choice: the son of Timaeus, Bartimaeus: the name means son of Timaeus
decisions.reason: Bar is Aramaic for son, so Mark explains the name. He gives the name perhaps because Bartimaeus was known to the first readers.

decisions.choice: a blind beggar by the road: begging from pilgrims on their way to the Passover
alternatives: a man without a home only
decisions.reason: Blind people often had no other way to live than begging. The road out of Jericho was busy with pilgrims going up to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the road: the same word as "the way"
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for Jesus' journey (10:32). At first Bartimaeus sits beside the way; in 10:52 he follows on it.

decisions.choice: which means son of Timaeus
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name in a short sentence.

records.source: καὶ ἀκούσας ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζαρηνός ἐστιν ἤρξατο κράζειν καὶ λέγειν· Υἱὲ Δαυὶδ Ἰησοῦ, ἐλέησόν με.
records.gloss: And having heard that Jesus the Nazarene it is, he began to cry out and to say, Son of David Jesus, have mercy on me.
pieces: When he heard it was Jesus of Nazareth, he started to shout, "Son of David, Jesus, have mercy on me!"

L.47: And when he heard that it was Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out and say, "Son of David, Jesus, have mercy on me!"

R.47: Bartimaeus heard that Jesus from Nazareth was passing by. So he began to shout, "Jesus, Son of David, show mercy to me!"

decisions.choice: Son of David: the King God promised from David's family
decisions.reason: God promised David a son whose kingdom would last forever (2 Samuel 7:12-16). By this time "Son of David" was a name for the Messiah. Only here in Mark is Jesus called by it, as he goes up to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: have mercy on me: show me kindness and help me
decisions.reason: The cry asks for pity and help, as people cried to God in the Psalms (Psalm 6:3).

decisions.choice: the Nazarene: the man from Nazareth
decisions.reason: The word names Jesus by his home town, as in 1:24.

decisions.choice: Jesus of Nazareth (B); Jesus from Nazareth (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where the name comes from.

records.source: καὶ ἐπετίμων αὐτῷ πολλοὶ ἵνα σιωπήσῃ· ὁ δὲ πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἔκραζεν· Υἱὲ Δαυίδ, ἐλέησόν με.
records.gloss: And were rebuking him many that he should be silent; but he much more kept crying out, Son of David, have mercy on me.
pieces: Many people scolded him and told him to keep quiet, but he kept shouting even more, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"

L.48: And many were rebuking him, [telling him] to be silent; but he kept crying out all the more, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"

R.48: Many people told him off and said, "Be quiet!" But he shouted even louder, "Son of David, show mercy to me!"

decisions.choice: were rebuking: sternly telling him to stop
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the disciples with the children (10:13).

decisions.choice: kept crying out all the more: an imperfect, he would not stop
decisions.reason: The tense pictures him shouting again and again, louder each time.

decisions.choice: said, "Be quiet!"
decisions.reason: Readable turns the order into the words spoken.

records.source: καὶ στὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Φωνήσατε αὐτόν.
records.gloss: And having stopped Jesus said, Call him.
pieces: Jesus stood still and said, "Call him over."

L.49: And Jesus stopped and said, "Call him."

R.49: Jesus stopped walking. He said, "Tell him to come here."

decisions.choice: stopped: stood still
decisions.reason: Jesus halts on his way to Jerusalem to answer the cry.

decisions.choice: call: summon
decisions.reason: The verb means to call someone to come. Mark uses it three times in 10:49.

records.source: καὶ φωνοῦσι τὸν τυφλὸν λέγοντες αὐτῷ· Θάρσει, ἔγειρε, φωνεῖ σε.
records.gloss: And they call the blind man saying to him, Take courage, rise up, he calls you.
pieces: So they called to the blind man and told him, "Take courage! Get up! He is calling you."

L.49: And they call the blind man, saying to him, "Take courage, get up; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is calling you."

R.49: So the people called the blind man. They said to him, "It is all right! Get up! Jesus is calling you."

decisions.choice: take courage: do not be afraid, be cheerful
decisions.reason: Jesus says the same word to the disciples on the lake (6:50).

decisions.choice: they call: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present again.

decisions.choice: they call, he calls: the crowd that silenced him now summons him
decisions.reason: The repeated verb shows the change in the crowd and Jesus' call to the man.

decisions.choice: Jesus is calling you
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἀποβαλὼν τὸ ἱμάτιον αὐτοῦ ἀναπηδήσας ἦλθεν πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν.
records.gloss: And having cast away the cloak of him, having jumped up he came to Jesus.
pieces: He threw off his cloak, sprang to his feet and came to Jesus.

L.50: And throwing off his cloak, he jumped up [and] came to Jesus.

R.50: Bartimaeus threw his coat to one side, jumped up and went to Jesus.

decisions.choice: cloak: the outer garment, a poor man's covering by day and night
decisions.reason: A beggar might spread his cloak to collect coins, and it was his blanket at night (Exodus 22:26-27). He leaves it behind in his eagerness.

decisions.choice: jumped up: leapt to his feet
decisions.reason: The verb shows his eagerness.

decisions.choice: coat
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday word for the outer garment.

records.source: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Τί σοι θέλεις ποιήσω;
records.gloss: And answering him Jesus said, What for you do you desire I should do?
pieces: Jesus said to him in reply, "What would you like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do for you?"

L.51: And Jesus answered him and said, "What do you want {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do for you?"

R.51: Jesus asked him, "What would you like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do for you?"

decisions.choice: what do you want me to do for you: the same question as in 10:36
decisions.reason: Jesus asked James and John the same thing. They asked for glory; this man asks for sight.

decisions.choice: answering: speaking in response to the man's cry
decisions.reason: Jesus responds to the man's coming.

records.source: ὁ δὲ τυφλὸς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ραββουνι, ἵνα ἀναβλέψω.
records.gloss: And the blind man said to him, Rabbouni, that I may see again.
pieces: The blind man said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Rabbouni, I want to see again."

L.51: And the blind man said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Rabbouni, [I want] to see again."

R.51: The blind man answered, "My Teacher, I want to be able to see again."

decisions.choice: Rabbouni: an Aramaic form of Rabbi, my master, my teacher
decisions.reason: The word is a fuller, more personal form of Rabbi. Mary Magdalene uses it of the risen Jesus in John 20:16.

decisions.choice: see again: regain sight, or look up
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to see again, as if he had once been able to see. It can also mean simply to look up or to gain sight.

decisions.choice: that I may see: a request with the main verb left out
decisions.reason: The words mean "I want to see" or "let me see".

decisions.choice: My Teacher
decisions.reason: Readable says what the title means, as it says "Teacher" for Rabbi.

records.source: καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ὕπαγε, ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε.
records.gloss: And Jesus said to him, Go, the faith of you has saved you.
pieces: Jesus told him, "Go. Your faith has saved you and made you well."

L.52: And Jesus said to him, "Go; your faith has saved you."

R.52: Jesus said to him, "Go. Your faith has made you well and saved you."

decisions.choice: has saved: has made well, and more
decisions.reason: The verb means both healing and rescue by God, as in 5:34. The man's sight is restored, and he follows Jesus on the way.

decisions.choice: faith: trust in Jesus to help him
decisions.reason: His faith was shown in his crying out and coming to Jesus. Jesus credits his faith, as he did the woman's in 5:34.

decisions.choice: go: you are free to go
decisions.reason: Jesus sends him on his way healed. He chooses to follow Jesus instead.

decisions.choice: saved you and made you well (B); made you well and saved you (R)
decisions.reason: As at 5:34, Balanced and Readable give both senses of the verb: the healing and the saving.

records.source: καὶ εὐθὺς ἀνέβλεψεν, καὶ ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ.
records.gloss: And immediately he received sight and he was following him on the road.
pieces: At once his sight came back, and he followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} along the road.

L.52: And immediately he saw again, and he was following {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on the way.

R.52: Right away the man could see again. He went with Jesus along the road and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: following him on the way: he becomes a disciple on the road to Jerusalem
alternatives: he walked behind for a while
decisions.reason: "Follow" is Mark's word for discipleship (1:18; 8:34), and "the way" is the road to Jerusalem and the cross (10:32). The healed man goes where Jesus goes.

decisions.choice: he saw again: a sight that the disciples still lack
decisions.reason: As with the blind man of 8:22-26, the healing closes a section in which the disciples fail to see what Jesus is teaching about his death.

decisions.choice: was following: an imperfect, he went on following
decisions.reason: The tense shows a continuing action.

decisions.choice: on the way (L); along the road (B, R)
alternatives: on the way at every level
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word that can also mean the way of discipleship. Balanced and Readable describe the road.
